items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: Wooden Joe, I used to play a little skacky job with them fellas, you know, like right there at the Claiborne and Tulane Avenue. They had a little spot there where he was playing.

ctx.x: But he could play trumpet. I never knew, if somebody told, mention the name of other, just, you knew what he was

about. Yeah, yeah, yeah, I tell ya, I tell ya, he was about, he played trumpet before Joe. I mean, he could play dance music. John Pendleton, he lived uptown, way uptown, too, on, I think he lived up on Pendleton Street. He lived up there. Way uptown. Yeah, yeah. And, uh, Joe Oliver had a repair shoe shop uptown. That's, he started, he had, you know, one of the little repair shoe shops. Well, Joe was playing, uh, brass band music. He could play the trumpet, but he couldn't play nothing but, uh, brass band. You…
Did you ever run with Wooden Joe much?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...Wooden Joe was in there playing clarinet... [INTERVIEWEE] Olavon and Wooden Joe. Yeah, well, no, he had a whole band.

ctx.x: Uh, well, you see, uh, they used to dance. They had, uh, they sell liquor there, you know, they had women working there, uh, hustling. And, uh, the fellas, people would come in there. Most of the men from off the ships, they'd come in there and spend money and dance. And go on and have a good time and put, uh, we had a kiddie box that we, that dropped the money in the kiddie box for the different numbers that they want to hear, you see. And, uh, now, uh, T-Net played, uh, the last I heard of him, he played with…

What about Abadese? Did you ever go by Abadese? Down there, I figured it was on the anvil. Well, it had another name and I can't remember. Something like the, the Princeton Inn or the Princeton Club or something like that. No, Joe Oliver used to be there with Big Eye Louie and Ernest Rogers and Wooden Joe was in there playing clarinet. Yeah. You know the place. That was the Magnolia band. No, I think Richard M. Jones was there. Not the Magnolia. Not the band that was on Hunts and Nagels, but another one. This is…

Olavon and Wooden Joe. Yeah, well, no, he had a whole band. Oh yeah, he had a whole band? Joe Oliver had a whole band. Mm-hm. Celestane. Joe Oliver had, he had Louis Kepard on the guitar, Pop Foster on the bass, and Willie Foster on the violin. That was Pop Foster's brother. And, uh, that's the, uh, the famous clarin, uh, clarinet and saxophone, uh, hot dog.
